assessment: Prior work has linked posterior urethral valves (PUV), a common cause of end stage renal disease in children, with chromosomal abnormalities and rare copy number variants, but the genetic causes of PUV remain incompletely defined. In this study, the authors have used a diverse ancestry whole-genome sequencing association study to identify two novel genes, TBX5 and PTK7, and an enrichment of rare duplications and inversions affecting candidate cis-regulatory elements as possible causes of this condition. These findings represent the first robust genetic associations of PUV, provide the foundation for developing a mechanistic understanding of the cause of this condition, and demonstrate how a diverse ancestry seqGWAS can be used for disease locus discovery in a rare disease.
